sandbox_and_permissions.external_side_effects: read-only access to the sibling repo $HOME/Projects/Claude template, exercised only by running its autopilot-update.sh (which reads that repo to copy files into this one). The Plexco session never writes to that sibling repo. A worktree/sandbox that cannot even READ that path cannot complete step 1 — but write access, which the earlier draft of this manifest required, is no longer needed.

focused: every one of the seven classification paths (genuinely-pending, stale, weak-probe, no-probe, manual-close well-formed, manual-close malformed-missing-reason, manual-close with no merged_probe at all) prints its own distinct, grep-stable marker line, exercised via a fixture backlog file containing one task block per path
a close_by: hand task is never added to the stale[] or weak[] arrays, so it can never cause --check to exit 1 and is never a candidate for --fix's flip loop
--fix leaves every close_by: hand task's status field byte-unchanged, independent of whether its probe currently matches origin/<default> or is symbol-shaped

a MALFORMED close_by declaration (missing/empty reason) grants NO exemption: when its underlying probe is independently stale or weak, the entry still lands in stale[]/weak[] and is still reported exactly as if close_by had never been written

the abuse guard fires when a close_by: hand task's scope list contains a file capable of carrying an identifier-shaped probe (application source under packages/*/src, apps/*/src, scripts/, or a new .sql migration) and does NOT fire when scope is limited to manifest/lockfile/workspace-config/doc files (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, docs/autopilot-manifests/*.json, *.md) — the deps-security-bump-shaped fixture (scope = docs manifest + package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml + pnpm-lock.yaml) must NOT trigger the guard

every existing classification path for a task block WITHOUT a close_by field is byte-identical to current output (regression) — the DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED / DEFAULT_BRANCH_MISSING HALT paths are untouched

the new scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile.test.sh never edits scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile; it only invokes the synced script as a subprocess against fixture backlog files and asserts stdout/exit code

after running autopilot-update.sh, scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile reads `# KIT_VERSION: 5` and is byte-identical to the template's current copy; if it still reads `4`, the template-side prerequisite has not landed

_verification_note: Stated as PROPERTIES, never literals — no pinned line count, no pinned task count from the live backlog. This manifest is hash-locked after register; a stale literal cannot be corrected in place and forces a full close-and-re-register cycle. Do NOT trust any number written anywhere in this repo's docs as a baseline: measure it at run time. No bash test harness (bats/shunit) exists in this repo today (grep found none 2026-07-30) — scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile.test.sh is this slice's own minimal fixture-based runner (build a temp backlog file per scenario, run the synced script against it, assert the exact marker line and exit code), so every focused-verification row above is re-runnable, not just narrated in a PR description.

security_review.reason: No trust boundary: local bash text-processing over a repo-tracked markdown file and git refs already trusted in this repo; no secrets, no network, no auth/permission/money surface, no external input. Reinforced by the repo split: the synced logic still lands in this slice's own diff and still gets a full codex-review-pin round, so nothing about the two-repo process removes review coverage.
security_review.void_if: the implementation is found to shell out to anything beyond git/awk/grep on local refs, or to read/write outside docs/autopilot-backlog.md and the scoped script/test files — if either happens, this judgement is void: add a security round and say why.

stop_conditions: AWAIT (not HALT) if, after running autopilot-update.sh, scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile still reads `# KIT_VERSION: 4` — the template-side half has not landed yet. This is a missing external prerequisite with a binary resume condition (template reads 5), not a defect of this slice; do not hand-author the v5 logic locally to work around it

a fourth close-by-hand-shaped task class is discovered beyond the three named (dependency-security, owner-evidence-gate, docs-reconcile) that does not fit the `close_by: hand · <reason>` shape — HALT and report; that would mean the escape hatch's shape is underspecified, an owner question, not an implementation choice

_acceptance.RCH-1: happy — close_by: hand + probe currently pending (no origin match) -> reported as manual-close, not the plain pending line, not added to stale/weak
_acceptance.RCH-2: happy — close_by: hand + probe matches origin but is NOT identifier-shaped (the real deps-security-bump-before-hand-flip shape) -> ⊘ manual-close, NOT WEAK-PROBE, not added to weak[]
_acceptance.RCH-3: happy — close_by: hand + probe matches origin AND happens to be identifier-shaped -> still ⊘ manual-close, never auto-flipped by --fix (declaration wins over auto-detection)
_acceptance.RCH-4: boundary — close_by: hand with reason missing or empty after the separator -> prints the exact three-line MALFORMED warning (see slice doc), same ✗ severity glyph as WEAK-PROBE because this is an authoring error, not a legitimate state
_acceptance.RCH-4b: boundary (the guarantee that matters) — a MALFORMED close_by grants NO exemption: falls back to the underlying stale/weak/no-probe/pending classification exactly as if close_by were never written, including counting toward stale[]/weak[] and --check's exit code when warranted. A broken field that loosens the rules is itself the back door
_acceptance.RCH-5: boundary — close_by: hand on a task with NO merged_probe at all -> routes to ⊘ manual-close (a human-only close is still a coherent declaration without a probe), not to the `?  no merged_probe` line
_acceptance.RCH-6 (abuse guard): close_by: hand + scope contains an application source path (packages/*/src, apps/*/src, scripts/*, or a new .sql) -> loud, non-silent warning distinct from manual-close, fires at least in --audit mode
_acceptance.RCH-7 (abuse guard negative): close_by: hand + scope limited to package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / pnpm-workspace.yaml / docs/autopilot-manifests/*.json / *.md -> no abuse warning (this is the deps-security-bump-shaped legitimate case; it must not be flagged)
_acceptance.RCH-8: --fix — a close_by: hand task's status line is byte-unchanged after --fix runs, in every one of RCH-1..RCH-3's preconditions
_acceptance.RCH-9: --check exit code — any number of well-formed close_by: hand entries never causes exit 1 on their own; only a genuine stale non-close_by entry does (a MALFORMED entry whose underlying probe is genuinely stale DOES still cause exit 1 — see RCH-4b)
_acceptance.RCH-10 (regression): every task block without a close_by field classifies identically to the current script's output, for all four existing categories (pending, stale, weak, no-probe) and both HALT paths (DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED, DEFAULT_BRANCH_MISSING)
_acceptance.RCH-11 (migration): diff contains no file under packages/db/migrations/ and no change to packages/db/schema.ts
_acceptance.RCH-12 (kit sync): after autopilot-update.sh runs, scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile is byte-identical to the canonical template file and both read `# KIT_VERSION: 5`; if the template still reads `4`, this is an AWAIT precondition failure, not a pass
_acceptance.RCH-13 (test isolation): scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile.test.sh contains no edit to scripts/autopilot-backlog-reconcile — it only invokes the synced script as a subprocess and asserts on its stdout/exit code

_evidence_rules: Cite acceptance rows by ID (RCH-N); do not restate their content in code comments — the restatement is what goes stale.
Docs and contracts are not runtime proof. A re-runnable fixture run against the actual script is.
